pairs.subject: concurrency-guards
pairs.evidence: src/i18n/catalog.ts:189 activate() writes `requested = lang` before the load and its rejection handler is a no-op, so after a failed locale load the gate stays held and the store's (unchanged) language re-activating it returns here, so that locale is wedged until the visitor picks a different one.

techniques.evidence: src/i18n/catalog.ts:204 The failure path of activate() swallows the error without resetting `requested`, so the gate acquired at line 190 is never released on rejection. The load caches do release on rejection (line 167), but this gate does not.
src/i18n/catalog.ts:159 Join policy: concurrent loadLocale callers share one in-flight promise per locale. The same shape is used for core and section loads.
src/i18n/catalog.ts:121 Section loads are keyed on (section id, locale). That is the deliberate identity: neither too broad nor per-request.
src/i18n/catalog.ts:200 A superseded locale load that resolves late is dropped instead of flipping the active catalog backwards.
src/i18n/catalog.ts:177 Registering a section twice does nothing, so module-scope re-evaluation is harmless.

src/i18n/catalog.ts:171 The shared promise handle is cached, but in the browser abandoned joiners' continuations still run, and a rejected handle is evicted at line 167. The technique's precondition (continuations torn down while the process lives) does not hold.

pairs.subject: concurrency-guards
pairs.evidence: src/lib/server/json-file-store.ts:60 The one publish door writes the temp file without flushing it and makes a single rename attempt. A Windows EPERM/EBUSY from a reader holding the destination is cleaned up and rethrown as a hard failure (lines 61-66) rather than classified as transient and retried under a bound, so a torn read becomes a lost update.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/server/json-file-store.ts:60 Conformant parts: same-directory temp, temp removed on failure, one door. Missing: no fsync before replace, no transient-error classification, no bounded retry, and exhaustion is not reported as a distinct failure.

src/lib/fileLock.ts:37 The guard is an in-process Map only. The header (lines 17-24) documents that multiple instances or workers both rename and the last one wins. The gap is acknowledged, not closed, and the store is scoped to local dev only by comment.
src/lib/fileLock.ts:44 One shared primitive with a per-key queue policy. Second callers run after the first, in call order.
src/lib/fileLock.ts:46 Release is structural. The wrapper takes the closure and the chain advances on both resolve and reject (lines 47-53), so a throwing body cannot wedge the key.
src/lib/server/json-file-store.ts:77 The read-modify-write deliberately holds one critical section across its awaits (read, update, write) instead of splitting it. That avoids the check-to-use race.

src/lib/server/json-file-store.ts:71 The guarded resource is the file, but its lock key is a separate free-form string that each call site supplies ('votes', 'waitlist', 'feature-boosts'...). Nothing ties the key to the file name or to one authority, so two writers of one file can use different keys and never collide.

pairs.subject: concurrency-guards
pairs.evidence: src/hooks/usePolling.ts:75 When the effect restarts (e.g. visibility hidden then visible, or a change to enabled or intervalMs), the new lifetime fires a tick immediately. The `cancelled` flag only stops the old lifetime from rescheduling, not its in-flight callback, so two callbacks can overlap.

techniques.evidence: src/hooks/usePolling.ts:75 Within one lifetime, ticks are serialized by scheduling after completion. Across lifetimes there is no in-flight guard, so a pending callback from the previous lifetime runs at the same time as the new one.
src/hooks/useAbortableEffect.ts:30 The abort and the timeout clear run in the effect cleanup, so every unmount or re-run path cancels the previous attempt.
